matches.quote: The weak-coupling BCS curve drawn in Fig. S2c has Delta(0) of about 0.3 meV, roughly four times smaller than the fitted values. ... reconcile them ... with STM gap values
The PCS model gives identical spectra for B2u and B3u, so the proposed B2u (SC2) to B3u (SC3) assignment comes entirely from the NMR of ref. 31.

The pressure determination (manometer, low-temperature calibration) is not described, nor is the pressure inhomogeneity. Inhomogeneity is invoked as one explanation for the double dips, so it should be quantified.
Fig. 1b-d: the role of the internodal vector q_N versus the reflection kz -> -kz is confusing. The ABS condition depends on the sign change ... not on q_N
Requested: fits with a general anisotropic Au state (independent Delta_x, Delta_y, Delta_z) using the same Gamma freedom as the B2u fits, with a quantitative goodness-of-fit comparison
What is not yet supported: (i) the nodal character, which is model-dependent, with Au not excluded;
The formalism assumes unitary d (d x d* = 0). This excludes the non-unitary and multicomponent states widely discussed for UTe2 (refs. 16, 24, 30, 31)
The authors should at least discuss how a cylindrical or realistic Fermi surface changes the distinction between pz-dominant and px(y)-dominant spectra, and ideally show a simulation for it.
Side dips flanking a conductance peak are the textbook signature of the contact region reaching its critical current... The heating test ... is not applied to the pressurised junction
Z goes from 1.67 to about 1.2 and Gamma from 0.39 meV to about 0.10 meV... So a change in the junction can masquerade as a change in Delta_z/Delta_x.
The two-channel superposition (Eqs. 2 and 3) at 1.0 to 1.2 GPa adds at least four more parameters. ... The weighted ratio <Delta_z>/<Delta_x(y)> then has no clear physical meaning
a transition between two different single-IR states along a second-order line is not generic. The lower-temperature phase would more naturally be a mixed state
The two-channel superposition (Eqs. 2 and 3) at 1.0 to 1.2 GPa adds at least four more parameters. It is motivated by either multiple gaps or pressure inhomogeneity
The ambient-pressure spectra of S1, S2 and S3 already differ among themselves by about as much as some pressure-induced changes do. S3 shows satellite structure at about +/-0.8 mV
The 1.4 GPa data are described but not fitted, and the ratio is not reported there. Since this pressure borders the MO phases, please state why
Only sample S1 was measured under pressure, and apparently with only one contact. ... Requested: ... at least one more independent junction measured under pressure.
It gives no estimate of contact size (Sharvin/Wexler) and no comparison with the electronic mean free path... It also gives no discussion of whether the contact is ballistic
Table S1 contradicts Fig. S7 and the main text. ... The column headers of Table S1 appear to be swapped.
The quoted uncertainties ... do not reflect parameter correlations. ... Please also give correlation matrices or chi^2 maps, and show that the minimum survives
Please state whether Z and Gamma were fixed in the temperature series (their values barely change in Figs. S7 and S8).

notes: C12 (B1u higher-order kx*ky*kz harmonic) is not matched to P15 because P15 critiques the spherical-FS / linear-in-k approximation for B2u/B3u rather than the exclusion of B1u. C19 (temperature-independent Gamma in Figs. S7-S8) is matched to P8, which notes the same constancy of Gamma across the temperature series and questions whether it was held fixed.
